To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hexapeptide sequence, LPXTGE, has been identified within 11 surface proteins from Gram-positive cocci and that it is located about 8-10 amino acids N-terminal from the C-terminal hydrophobic domain that is found in all surface proteins from these cocci.
a highly conserved hexa‐peptide sequence (both protein and DNA level) has identified in 11 surface proteins from Gram-positive cocci.
a hexapeptide is conserved in all known surface proteins from the Gram‐positive cocci.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of surface‐specific proteins of Gram‐positive cocci and their role in the attachment of these organisms to surfaces.
the structure and function of bacterial cell wall proteins.

the identification and characterisation of surface proteins from various Gram‐positive bacteria, and in the case of Staphylococcus aureus, with the identification and cloning of genes encoding these proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hexapeptide LPXTGE is a highly conserved sequence in the C‐terminal region of all Gram‐positive surface proteins.
the LPXTGE sequence is a general feature of surface proteins from gram‐positive bacteria.
the LPXTG‐type motif represents the attachment site for all Gram‐positive surface proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is a very interesting and important area of research.
this hexapeptide sequence is a conserved feature of Gram‐positive bacterial surface proteins.
this sequence, LPXTGE, has a role in anchoring the surface protein to the cell wall.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hexapeptide sequence LPXTG is found in the cell wall anchor domains of many surface proteins in Gram-positive bacteria.
the LPXTG sequence motif is highly conserved in all surface proteins from Gram-positive bacteria and it is essential for anchoring of surface proteins to the peptidoglycan layer.
the hexapeptide is an important feature for the anchoring of surface proteins to the cell wall of Gram‐positive bacteria.
